reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Absent tonsils plus very low immunoglobulins in a boy means Bruton disease
Catalase positive abscesses suggest chronic granulomatous disease
DiGeorge links T cell deficiency with heart defects and hypocalcaemia
CD4 count predicts which HIV opportunist appears
reference.pathophysiology: Gene defects arrest lymphocyte development, signalling or microbial killing at defined checkpoints. HIV binds CD4 with coreceptors, integrates into host DNA and progressively destroys helper T cells, collapsing cell mediated immunity while chronic activation exhausts remaining clones.
additionalDifferentials: Antibody versus combined immunodeficiency by infection pattern
Bruton disease versus common variable immunodeficiency
Primary deficiency versus HIV acquired deficiency
additionalInvestigations: Neutrophil oxidative burst testing for granulomatous disease
HIV antigen antibody testing with CD4 count and viral load
